newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK PSBR data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK PSBR data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK PSBR data published at 0930 GMT.
The PSBR showed a net repayment of 4.4 billion stg in October versus expectations of a 1.9 bln stg repayment.

"This is a very favourable figure. The only question is how much January's corporation tax payment will be reduced correspondingly due to today's figure. With that proviso, the backdrop for the Chancellor going into the budget is very buoyant."

"The largest UK PSDR on record suggests that worries about an overshoot on the PSBR this year are not justified. However, the much larger than expected debt repayment also argues against any tax cuts in the in the upcoming budget. Very strong tax receipts, especially out of the corporate sector, provide additional evidence of the buoyancy of the economy at the start of the quarter and hence, the lack of and need for further stimulus."

"There is no doubt this gives the Chancellor a little bit more room for manoeuvre although he would prefer a relatively cautious budget this time round if only to minimise the chances of interest rates going up too sharply ahead of the election. I think we will see some tax cuts (in the upcoming budget), certainly in gross terms we will see a reduction in the basic rate."

"Certainly a very, very good figure indeed for the Chancellor. Although it makes it much more likely the Chancellor will hit his target for PSBR for the current fiscal year, we don't believe he'll be tempted to cut taxes by anything more than 3 billion pounds."
